audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

harness_api.quote: Use humanlayer automation run to run one Cloud-visible coding session from any automation environment — a CI job, a cron machine, or a script on a server.
harness_api.note: First-party control plane for harnesses on your hosts: app.humanlayer.com (web/mobile/desktop) creates sessions on a chosen daemon host, streams session events and sends follow-up messages; the CLI (`humanlayer automation run --pat ... --prompt/--prompt-file --coding-agent --model`) starts a prompted session headlessly and lets you follow up from Cloud. Harnesses: Claude Code (Claude Agent SDK), Codex, plus HumanLayer's own Fold agent (preview). The HumanLayer API itself is not documented as a public REST API/SDK; the documented programmatic surface is the CLI. It drives agents on your own machines, not provider sandboxes.

egress_allowlist.quote: The daemon gives coding agents the file and network access of the user that runs it. Use an account with only the access that the sessions need.
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side network controls; you restrict the host yourself.

egress_http_rules.quote: The daemon gives coding agents the file and network access of the user that runs it.
egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side egress layer at all (BYO compute).

secret_proxy.quote: The coding agent also needs its provider credential in the environment — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the default Claude setup.
secret_proxy.note: BYOK: model keys/subscriptions live on the daemon host (env vars, `claude /login`), workspace config copies .env files into worktrees; no injecting proxy.

windows.quote: Run a remote daemon: run HumanLayer on Linux, Windows, a remote machine, or a private-network host.
windows.note: The HumanLayer daemon runs on a Windows host you bring; not a Windows machine HumanLayer provides

macos.note: Desktop app / daemon installable via Homebrew on macOS; runs on your own Mac, not a HumanLayer-provided macOS machine

max_session_h.quote: The host can be a cloud VM, workstation, or private-network machine. Select a host that can access the code, tools, credentials, and private services that the agent needs.
max_session_h.note: Since HumanLayer runs on compute you bring and control, there is no HumanLayer-imposed session time limit; the host you choose determines runtime

docker_inside.quote: Credentials remain available when you stop and restart the same container. ... This Compose service fragment stores credentials in a named volume: services: daemon: environment: HUMANLAYER_RIPTIDE_HOME: /var/lib/humanlayer volumes: - humanlayer-auth:/var/lib/humanlayer
docker_inside.note: Docs document running the HumanLayer daemon itself inside a Docker container via Docker Compose.

persistent_disk.quote: Bring your own compute, development environment, and agent harness, or run the HumanLayer stack on your workstation or remote workers.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. HumanLayer does not host or manage machines/disks itself (BYO compute); any disk persistence is a property of the customer's own host, not a HumanLayer feature.

mcp_server.quote: Turn any MCP server into a CLI for easy use with subagents
mcp_server.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. HumanLayer's GitHub org ships an MCP-to-CLI adapter tool, not an MCP server for controlling HumanLayer sandboxes/machines (HumanLayer has no sandbox compute of its own to expose via MCP).

lang_python.quote: HumanLayer is a multiplayer coding agent IDE and cloud that works seamlessly from your workstation to anywhere you want to run background agents. ... Bring your own compute, development environment, and agent harness.
lang_python.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The current product is a control plane/CLI (Node-based) for orchestrating coding-agent sessions on customer-owned hosts; it does not itself provide a Python runtime or code-exec sandbox. (A legacy PyPI `humanlayer` SDK exists but belongs to the deprecated pre-pivot human-approval product, not the current agent-workspace product this card models.)

lang_node.quote: HumanLayer CLI — daemon management and authentication
lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Node.js is a prerequisite for installing the `@humanlayer/cli` tool itself (npm install -g @humanlayer/cli), but HumanLayer does not provide a hosted Node runtime/sandbox for user code; execution happens on the customer's own host.

arm64.note: Official desktop app cask ships a darwin-arm64 build; the CLI (npm package) also runs on ARM Linux hosts.

hipaa.quote: Security SOC 2 Type II HumanLayer is SOC 2 Type II compliant. We use Vanta to help monitor our security controls and maintain compliance. ZDR and DPA agreements available on enterprise tiers.
hipaa.note: The security section states SOC 2 Type II, ZDR, and DPA availability but makes no mention of HIPAA eligibility or BAAs anywhere on the pricing/security/enterprise copy.

eu_data_residency.quote: HumanLayer runs two production-grade environments that are ready for SOC 2 customer data. Beta uses *.codelayer.cloud. Production uses *.humanlayer.com.
eu_data_residency.note: Only a single production environment (humanlayer.com) and a beta environment are documented; no EU/region choice or data-residency option is mentioned anywhere in the docs or pricing/security pages.

open_source.quote: public issues repo for humanlayer - the code here is pretty much all deprecated - you can try the rebuild of humanlayer at https://humanlayer.com - thanks for all your support - dex
open_source.note: The org's original humanlayer/humanlayer repo (linked as the official GitHub from docs.humanlayer.com) is explicitly deprecated by the founder, who says the current product is 'the rebuild ... at https://humanlayer.com' -- i.e. the live Cloud/daemon product being reviewed is not published there. Other org repos (12-factor-agents, skills, agentcontrolplane, fold) are open-source side projects/agent tooling, not the core HumanLayer Cloud sandbox/session product itself, so they don't establish the core product as open source. No official page states the current HumanLayer Cloud product is open source; confirms the 'no'.
